## heading for Local 100.11

problem: Local 100.11
argument: P->P . P  .: P
comment: This is a perfectly correct application of MP.  The fact that the rule is stated using distinct antecedent and consequent allows the antecedent and consequent to be distinct, but does not require it.

problem: Recog 1.010
argument: T->S  .: ~~(T->S)
comment: As in 1.007, the "official" outermost parentheses have been dropped in the premise, but cannot be dropped in the conclusion.
## heading for Local 82.11

problem: Local 82.11
argument: R->Q  .: ~~R->Q
comment: Compare 1.014.  The premise, in official notation, is \l"(R->Q)"\l; the conclusion is \l"(~~R->Q)"\l.  This is not a correct application of DN.

problem: x.Z 27
argument: P->Q  .: P->Q|R
comment: Like 1.006, this attempt at Addition miscarries because of the lack of parentheses in the conclusion.  A correct application of ADD (more precisely ADDR) would yield \l"(P->Q)|R"\l.
## heading for Local 64.11

problem: Local 64.11
argument: (P|Q)->R . ~P  .: Q
comment: One can't just ignore the \l"->R"\l.

problem: Recog 3.003
argument: Gx  .: forall x Gx
comment: There is no inference rule, UG, for universally generalizing a formula.  Instead, we have Universal Derivation (UD) as a new form for boxing & canceling.
## heading for Local 46.11

problem: Local 46.11
argument: ~forall x exists y (Fz<->Gy)  .: exists z ~exists y (Fz<->Gy)
comment: This appears to be an attempt to apply QN, but the rewriting of the variable "x" to "z" prevents this from being a correct application of QN.

problem: x.Z 63
argument: exists z (FA&Gy)->exists x Hx|GA  .: exists x (exists z (Fx&Gy)->exists x Hx|Gx)
comment: Exactly like 3.020 except that both occurrences of "A" were generalized on.
## heading for Local 28.11

problem: Local 28.11
argument: forall x (Fx->exists y (FB&Gy))  .: forall x (Fx->exists z exists y (Fz&Gy))
comment: This appears to be an attempt to apply EG to the interior of a formula, in fact, to just the consequent of the inner conditional (with "B" as the instantial term, and "z" as the generalized variable).

problem: Recog 4.006
argument: forall x exists z F(A(xyx)z)  .: exists z F(A(CyC)z)
## heading for Local 10.11

problem: Local 10.11
argument: forall x FA(xB(y))|G(Cy)  .: exists w (forall x FA(xw)|G(Cy))

problem: x.Z 99
argument: exists z G(xzx) . y=x .: exists z G(yzy)
correct-rules: LL.LL2
comment: This is a correct application of LL, in particular of LL2.  In Command Mode, there would be a query as to which of the (free) occurrences of "x" you wish to replace by "y".  The answer here was "both of them".
## heading for Local -8.11

problem: Local -8.11
argument: A(x)=B(x) .: C(A(x)B(x))=C(B(x)B(x))
correct-rules: EL
comment: This is a correct application of EL.  Here the complex term into which the replacement is being made is "C( __ B(x))", with "C" a 2-place operation symbol, and "B" a 1-place operation symbol.  If you prove T305 to derive EL from LL and SID, you may see more clearly why EL, like LL1, allows you to replace any number of the (free) occurrences of the premise's left-hand term by (free) occurrences of the premise's right-hand term.
